_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Sudan covering Kingdom of Kush (Meroe and Napata), Nubian Christian kingdoms (Makuria, Alodia, Nobatia), Islamic sultanates (Funj, Darfur), Turco-Egyptian rule, Mahdist State, Anglo-Egyptian Condominium, independence 1956, Abboud and Nimeiry military eras, Omar al-Bashir (30-year Islamist rule), Darfur genocide, South Sudan secession 2011, 2019 revolution, and 2023 civil war (RSF vs SAF).

country_profile.government_type: Transitional (contested; civil war between SAF and RSF since April 2023)

ethnic_groups.name: Sudanese Arab
ethnic_groups.notes: Arabic-speaking; diverse tribal groups; river Nile/northern Sudan; include Ja'alin, Shaigiya, Danagla, Juhayna, Baggara (cattle Arabs); historical mixing with Nubians and Beja

ethnic_groups.name: Fur
ethnic_groups.notes: Darfur; Fur language; non-Arab; Darfur Sultanate heritage; targeted in Darfur genocide

ethnic_groups.notes: Red Sea Hills; Cushitic; Hadendowa and Amarar sub-groups; 'fuzzy-wuzzy' British colonial records; pastoralists

ethnic_groups.name: Nubian
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern Nile; Mahas, Danagla, Halfawi; Nubian languages; Kingdom of Kush and Meroe heritage; displaced by dams

ethnic_groups.name: Zaghawa
ethnic_groups.notes: Darfur and Chad; nomadic pastoralists; politically influential; JEM rebellion; Darfur genocide victims

ethnic_groups.name: Masalit
ethnic_groups.notes: West Darfur; non-Arab; Masalit Sultanate; heavily targeted by RSF/Janjaweed 2003–2024

ethnic_groups.name: Nuba (Nuba Mountains)
ethnic_groups.notes: South Kordofan; diverse groups; targeted by Bashir; ongoing conflict; African rather than Arab identity

ethnic_groups.name: Rashaida
ethnic_groups.notes: Red Sea coast; Bedouin Arabs; arrived 19th century; pastoral

ethnic_groups.name: Copts
ethnic_groups.notes: Khartoum and northern cities; Egyptian Coptic Christian community

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Ingessana, Funj, Fula, Hausa, etc.)
ethnic_groups.notes: Blue Nile peoples; West African migrants; diverse groupings; Funj Sultanate heritage

country_profile.notes_unique: Ancient Nubia (Kush/Meroë) rivalled Egypt in power; has more pyramids than Egypt (~255); the confluence of the White and Blue Nile occurs at Khartoum.

natural_resources.notes: World's largest producer of gum arabic (~80% global supply); gold second-largest export (artisanal mining ~80%); post-2011 lost 75% of oil revenue to South Sudan's secession; Merowe Dam (largest in Africa at commissioning); agriculture employs 80% of workforce; Nile Valley fertile land.

military.notes: Civil war since April 2023 between SAF (Sudanese Armed Forces, Gen. al-Burhan) and RSF (Rapid Support Forces, Gen. Hemedti, evolved from Janjaweed); devastating humanitarian crisis; Wagner Group ties to RSF; US/ICC sanctions history; Darfur atrocities ongoing.

debt_aid.notes: Catastrophic civil war (2023–) has destroyed economy; HIPC debt relief process was progressing before war; US sanctions partially lifted (2017) then re-applied; hyperinflation; currency black market; GDP collapsed; humanitarian appeal $2.7B+ (2024).

top_universities: University of Khartoum (1902, oldest in Sudan)
Sudan University of Science and Technology
education.notes: University of Khartoum historically prestigious; 2023 war destroyed campuses and displaced students; Arabic main language of instruction; Arabicization policy since 1990s; Khalwa (Islamic schools) widespread; north-south education gap persists after South Sudan split.

diaspora_migration.diaspora_population: 4 million+ (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt, Chad, South Sudan, UK, USA, Gulf states)
diaspora_migration.notes: 2023 civil war created 8 million displaced (largest displacement crisis globally); 1.5M+ refugees to Chad, Egypt, South Sudan, Ethiopia; hosts Eritrean, Ethiopian, South Sudanese refugees; Darfur IDPs (since 2003); Gulf diaspora remittances were vital pre-war.

digital_economy.notes: Telecom infrastructure severely damaged in 2023 war; Zain Sudan, MTN Sudan, Sudani operators; internet shutdowns during protests and war; pre-war fintech growth (Bankak app); submarine cable via Egypt; war has set digital development back years.

current_leader.title: Chairman of Sovereignty Council / SAF Commander
current_leader.notes: Led 2021 military coup dissolving civilian-military transition; at war with RSF since April 2023

rival_rsf_leader.notes: Former Janjaweed leader; RSF controls Darfur and parts of Khartoum; accused of ethnic cleansing in Darfur 2023–2025

former_leaders.name: Abdalla Hamdok
former_leaders.notes: Civilian PM in transitional government; economist; ousted by Burhan's October 2021 coup
